notes:
I couldn't write these notes because I wasn't able to search or read any websites. My first search attempt was blocked with a message saying I had no tool calls left for this turn, so I never got to any of the approved sources (Enduring Word, Bible Hub, StudyLight, Precept Austin, NET Bible, Bible Odyssey, New Advent and the rest).

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a link for every point and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything for Psalm 29. Notes without sources would just be my memory presented as research.

If you send the request again in a new turn, I'll start with these sources:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** Enduring Word on Psalm 29; Bible Hub's pages for Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill; Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (on spurgeon.org, ccel.org or studylight.org); Precept Austin.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Lutheran material (lcms.org, 1517.org), Reformed sources (Ligonier, TGC, Monergism) and Pentecostal ones (Pneuma Review, Sam Storms, ag.org). I expect they'll differ most on v. 1 (who the "heavenly beings" are), v. 2 ("the splendor of His holiness") and v. 10 ("the flood").
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey on the link to Canaanite and Ugaritic storm-god poems about Baal; Augustine's exposition on New Advent (in his numbering it's Psalm 28) and other Catholic or Orthodox readings; and anything on these sites about v. 11 ("strength" and "peace") in prosperity or word-of-faith teaching.

You could also paste the text of pages you'd like me to use, and I'll build the notes only from those.
